question: Can a fixed reference DEFLATE compressor predict enough of an original gzip stream's exact token syntax that plaintext plus a compact correction stream beats the original gzip bytes?
predictor: Python runtime zlib 1.3, raw DEFLATE, level 6, default strategy, generated from the restored plaintext. The exact version string is stored and decoding rejects a mismatch. This is a deliberate non-portable research limitation.
representation: DCP1 includes magic, pinned zlib version, compressed plaintext (xz preset 1), original gzip header/trailer, original block/tree/padding metadata, and token corrections. At each original token output offset, a P tag uses an identical reference token; L derives an original literal from the plaintext; M stores the full original length-code/extra and distance-code/extra syntax; E marks block end. Stored blocks preserve their bytes. All sizes count.
controls: GZB1 plus zlib level 9 over gzip bytes
GXB1 plus xz preset 1 over gzip bytes
validation: Byte-exact stored/fixed/dynamic synthetic gzip cases first. Every real DCP1 case must rebuild identical gzip bytes and semantic plaintext. A smaller complete candidate must also pass a fresh-process archive-only inverse check.
stop: One fixed screen only. No parameter search, production route, novelty claim, or claim that this exhausts advanced preflate-style predictors.
